evidence: Two top-level packages (coursera, coursera.test) with clear separation of core logic and tests
Organized domain-specific modules (api.py, cookies.py, downloaders.py, workflow.py) grouped by responsibility rather than by technical layer
Strong inter-module dependencies (e.g., workflow.py imports from formatting.py, downloaders.py, filtering.py), indicating internal cohesion without strict layering
No explicit separation into layers (e.g., no 'presentation/', 'service/', 'persistence/' directories)
Code structure follows high cohesion and low coupling principles typical of a modular monolith
Presence of distinct subsystems like API clients, downloaders, extractors, and workflow controllers with limited cross-cutting concerns
Test directory mirrors the source structure (test_api.py → api.py), supporting modular testing
Average fan-out of ~5.9 indicates moderate cross-module communication, inconsistent with layered architecture (low fan-out between layers) but typical in modular monolith
risks: Tight coupling between modules may reduce maintainability as system evolves
Limited modularity boundaries could hinder independent deployment or technology evolution
The flat directory structure (depth 3) with many modules at same level may become unwieldy at scale
